subject: Edge region attestation: APAC private endpoint & operator access confirmation
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@zenhealth.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: Lina Moreno <lina.m@zenhealth.com>, security@zenhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC edge residency controls and private endpoint attestation

Chloe —

We're starting our internal security review for the pilot that will put sensitive PHI-adjacent inference traffic into a Red-Hosted APAC edge zone. Before we proceed with the PO, we need a short attestation and a few artifacts to show our InfoSec and cloud ops teams. Specifically: 

1) Confirmation that the APAC edge region will only host tenant data for customers selecting APAC residency (no cross-border failover without explicit opt-in).
2) Details on VPC/private endpoint connectivity: does traffic traverse public internet at any point? Any requirement for private peering/Direct Connect?
3) Key management: where are tenant keys stored for the APAC edge? Is there an operator-facing KMS?
4) Operator access & change control: steps to request on-call access to the edge operator console; are there dedicated operator accounts per customer?
5) Evidence artifacts: CAIQ/SIG pointers or a condensed artifact pack we can drop into our audit workspace (we only need a 1–2 page summary + diagrams).

If you can provide a short attestation letter and a network diagram + runbook excerpt that lists the allowed egress ranges, that will get our engineers unblocked. Happy to take these over a secure drive link.

Thanks —
Sanjay
Principal Security Engineer
ZenHealth


From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@zenhealth.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC edge residency controls and private endpoint attestation

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can provide an attestation and a concise artifact packet. Quick answers up front:

- Residency: APAC edge zones are opt-in by account and will not fail over cross-region unless you explicitly enable geo-fallback in the account settings.
- Connectivity: Traffic to the edge private endpoint can be restricted to private peering (VPC peering / PrivateLink equivalent); by default the endpoint is accessible via TLS over a private circuit when a peering is configured. No public internet egress is required for customer traffic.
- KMS: Tenant-level keys for APAC-hosted workloads are stored in the APAC key partition of our managed KMS; we can provide a KMS partition diagram and key lifecycle notes. No operator access to raw key material; operator actions are audited.
- Operator access: Access is via SSO + Just-In-Time (JIT) approval for emergency access. Non-emergency operator work is done via sealed automation runbooks.

I'm looping in Irene (security/compliance) and Marissa (hosting ops) to attach the diagram and an ops-runbook excerpt that lists the published egress ranges and the on-call escalation flow. Expect a follow-up with the artifact links in <24 hours.

Best,
Chloe
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Lina Moreno <lina.m@zenhealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@zenhealth.com>, security@zenhealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC edge residency controls and private endpoint attestation

Chloe —

Thanks for the rapid reply. A couple of clarifying follow-ups from our network team before we accept the artifact pack:

- IP allowlist: can you confirm the exact IPv4/IPv6 ranges for the APAC edge endpoints (or provide a CIDR list we can drop into our firewall rules)?
- SLA & failover: if the APAC edge becomes unhealthy, what is the default behavior? Is there an automatic failover to another Redwood region or does traffic queue? We need to document this for our risk register.
- Operator audit logs: will you be able to provide a sample of the audit log format (timestamped events) or a sanitized extract?

We appreciate the runbook excerpt — that should help our ops folks triage. One more ask: can you provide a one-page signed attestation (PDF) stating the residency guarantees and the statement that operator access is audited and limited?

Thanks,
Lina
Security Engineering Manager
ZenHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@zenhealth.com>, Lina Moreno <lina.m@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC edge residency controls and private endpoint attestation

Hi Lina / Sanjay —

Appreciate the precision here. Attaching the two artifacts you asked for and answering the bullets below. Attachments: redwood_edge_vpc_diagram_v2.pdf (network diagram, includes CIDRs), ops-runbook-edge-apac.md (runbook excerpt + audit example).

Answers:
- IP allowlist: see diagram appendix A — published IPv4 ranges: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24; IPv6: 2001:db8::/48. These are the stable front-door ranges for the APAC private endpoints; we publish a weekly update to the linked Drive folder if ranges change.
- SLA & failover: default is to fail closed for residency-sensitive accounts (traffic does not automatically route cross-region). For accounts that opt into geo-fallback, the policy is explicit and must be enabled in the account settings; in that mode the traffic will fail over to the secondary region with a best-effort degraded SLA. We will include the exact failover timers in the attestation PDF.
- Operator audit logs: included in ops-runbook-edge-apac.md is a sanitized sample event stream (JSON lines) showing JIT access approvals, session start/stop, and operator commands. We can provide a signed hash of a longer sample under an NDA if you need a full slice.

We also created the requested one-page attestation PDF (linked in Drive) that states residency guarantees, KMS partitioning, and the operator audit controls. If you'd like this on company letterhead with an exec signature we can route to Legal for signing (48–72 hour turnaround).

Next steps: 
- I'll add the Drive link in a separate email thread with download ACLs.
- If ZenHealth wants to proceed with private peering, our network team can propose a peering template and a target cutover window.

If there's anything else you need to move the PO forward, ping me and we'll prioritize.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Hosting Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
